Replay

Carrier death, disconnect and recovery

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
What is still differentCompatibility and acceptance

C7 retains relic ownership through carrier death, revive and automatic respawn. The relic remains attached to a connected avatar at (10, -12). A disconnected carrier keeps ownership and version, while the relic stays at its last recorded position. Rejoining with that reserved identity resumes attachment. Another player cannot grab the still-owned relic. Restart explicitly releases it.

These rules follow the original carry loop and session departure handling: scripts/cavecrawl.odin attaches without an HP gate, its player_left hooks only report departure, and Kit's session.mark_left retains entity ownership. The original UI prevents a dead player from issuing gameplay controls, as Replay's action predicate does. Replay previously cleared relic ownership on its first dead/disconnected tick, including temporary membership loss during recovery.

Replay can explicitly replace a reserved seat with a different identity. Its reset_player releases that seat's relic at the existing position, advancing the version once. This prevents a new occupant from inheriting a former player's possession. Ordinary rejoin does not call this identity-reset path.

What is still different#

Replay computes attachment in the simulation. Original Kit streams owner poses. A disconnected Replay avatar may move to a new floor under the existing reserved avatar policy; the parked relic does not follow until the carrier returns. Original floor progression includes disconnected avatar bodies in its gate.

C8 now adopts the old host’s relic on a recorded authority change, matching Kit’s non-avatar orphan sweep. Successor/guest carriers retain ownership. Owner-streamed pose behavior and the disconnected-body floor gate remain separate comparison boundaries.

Compatibility and acceptance#

Current content is 0x4341564552504c39. Convert C1–C8 archives explicitly with tools/upgrade_save and a new destination. C6 conversion preserves the complete saved frame and peer ledger; it cannot reconstruct a carrier already cleared by old gameplay. C8 adds authority-observation fields to the world; network/checkpoint envelope versions are unchanged. Conversion seeds those fields from the validated checkpoint’s host-seat metadata.

The acceptance runner covers actual death/revive/respawn, disconnect/rejoin and identity replacement in the model, complete corrected-input frame/event equality, archived-state conversion, native retained frames, and carrier movement/release after planned or crashed-host recovery. The browser variant carries the relic through the existing RTC party, loot, door, social and handoff story.
